name: Faded Pink
lede: Faded Pink is a dusty, muted rose, built from the modifier "faded" laid onto ordinary pink rather than from any single dated source.

sections.title: A modifier, not a coinage
sections.body:
Three separate sources in our library land on close to this same hex: the 2010 xkcd survey, Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature*, and the ISCC-NBS 1955 dictionary [1]. Ridgway's plate XXXVIII gives a near match at hue 69, tone d, read from a scan of an aged printed plate, so the match is approximate, not exact [1]. ISCC-NBS 1955 files the same patch of color space as block 251, a moderate purplish pink [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[laelia-pink]], [[mauvelous]], [[alizarine-pink]] and [[pig-pink]], at 3, 3.9, 4 and 4.7 ΔE [1]. A near-duplicate in our data, Persian Lilac, sits about 1.1 units away, close enough that the two names likely describe the same swatch to most eyes [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, carries this color in just 4 paintings at five percent coverage or more [3]. The earliest is Lucas van Leyden's 1531 [[painting:commons-Q117196346|Healing of the Blind Man of Jericho]], where it covers about 7 percent of the panel [3]. It also turns up in Henri Matisse's 1908 [[painting:commons-Q21723020|Nymph and Satyr]] and Raimundo de Madrazo y Garreta's 1877 [[painting:commons-Q27780861|Manuela de Errazu]], both well below that share [3]. These are museum photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is a screen color, not a pigment identification [3].
